title: Nut-Free Peach & Cream Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft peach cupcakes with fresh peach puree frosting, ready in about 43 minutes total with 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes taste like a peach cobbler turned into a handheld treat. I tested this recipe on a hot July afternoon using peaches from my neighbor's tree, and the batter smelled like summer before it even hit the oven. The cake stays soft because real peach puree goes into the batter, not just extract. That puree adds moisture and a light golden color without any nuts hiding in the mix. The frosting is where this recipe gets its main flavor. Fresh peach puree gets folded into a simple butter frosting, so every bite tastes like ripe fruit instead of sugar alone. This batch is fully nut-free, so it works for school events, potlucks, or any party where allergies are a concern.
ingredients: 1/2 cup fresh peach puree (about 1 large ripe peach, peeled)
1 cup unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
1/3 cup fresh peach puree, strained through a fine mesh sieve
thin fresh peach slices, for garnish (optional)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F and line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Peel and puree one large ripe peach in a blender until smooth. Set aside 1 cup total, divided for cake and frosting.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt in a medium bowl. Set aside.
Beat 1/2 cup butter and granulated sugar together until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, then mix in vanilla and 1/2 cup peach puree until combined.
Alternate adding the flour mix and milk to the butter mix, starting and ending with flour. Mix just until smooth.
Divide batter evenly among the liners, filling each about two thirds full. Bake for 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool cupcakes in the pan for 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool fully before frosting.
For the frosting, beat 1 cup butter until smooth, then add powdered sugar in two batches.
Mix in the strained peach puree, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt. Beat on high for 2 minutes until fluffy.
Pipe frosting onto cooled cupcakes and top with a thin peach slice if you like.
tips: Strain the frosting puree well. Extra liquid can make the frosting too soft to pipe high swirls.
Use very ripe, fragrant peaches. Firm peaches give less flavor and less color to the batter.
Chill the frosting for 10 minutes before piping if your kitchen is warm, since real fruit softens buttercream fast.
Make the peach puree a day ahead and keep it covered in the fridge to save prep time.

faq.question: Can I use canned peaches instead of fresh?
faq.answer: Yes, but drain canned peaches well and pat them dry before pureeing. Canned peaches carry more liquid, so cut back the milk in the batter by 1 tablespoon.

faq.question: Why is my peach frosting runny?
faq.answer: The puree likely had too much liquid. Strain it through a fine mesh sieve and add extra powdered sugar, 2 tablespoons at a time, until it firms up.

faq.question: Can I make these cupcakes ahead for a party?
faq.answer: Bake the cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store them unfrosted at room temperature in a sealed container. Frost them the morning of the party for the freshest peach flavor.

faq.question: Do I need to peel the peaches?
faq.answer: Yes, peeling gives a smoother puree and a cleaner color in both the cake and frosting. Blanch peaches in boiling water for 30 seconds to make peeling easier.

conclusion: These peach and cream cupcakes are a simple way to use ripe summer peaches in something other than pie. The real fruit puree in both cake and frosting keeps the flavor honest and the texture soft. Bring these to your next warm weather gathering and watch the plate empty fast.
